newsitem.title: USA: US VP Gore says meeting with Congress "excellent".
newsitem.headline: US VP Gore says meeting with Congress "excellent".

text.p: Vice President Al Gore Tuesday said a meeting between Congressional leaders and President Clinton was "excellent," and they hoped to work in a bipartisan manner on a number of issues, including taxes.

The White House and Republican leaders in Congress generally agreed to aim for a bipartisan approach on taxes, he said after the meeting at the Capitol. "Tax issues that both sides have put forward were discussed and there was general agreement that there would be an effort to create a bipartisan approach to see how we could deal with those issues within the context of a balanced budget agreement," Gore said.
Asked whether the Clinton administration was ready to accept a broad-based capital gains tax cut, Gore said there was "no indication" of that.

Gore said bipartisan working groups would be developed on five key issues, to which Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle, a Democrat from South Dakota, wanted to add the issue of children's health care. But Gore said although Republicans did not reject that outright, they did not appear ready to add it to the list.
"We've set out a process that I think can work," Daschle told reporters.
